world.title: Disclosure of home address helped prompt US Treasury chief
world.summary: Media reports that helped identify U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s Washington-area home partly prompted his move to a military base, a source familiar with the relocation told The Associated Press. The account adds an explanation for the security measure first reported earlier this week. The source said disclos
world.content: Media reports that helped identify U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s Washington-area home partly prompted his move to a military base, a source familiar with the relocation told The Associated Press. The account adds an explanation for the security measure first reported earlier this week. The source said disclosure of his address contributed to the decision. The Wall Street Journal had published an aerial photograph of Bessent’s Georgetown home that another source said could be geolocated. Bessent has led President Donald Trump’s economic pressure campaign against Iran, Operation Economic Outcast, since August. A Treasury Department spokesperson said he would continue the campaign and the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports despite threats against him. A senior U.S. intelligence official warned in a memo last month that Iranian plots against U.S. personnel and citizens had reached an “advanced stage,” though officials have not publicly detailed the specific threats to Bessent. Iran has denied plotting attacks on U.S. officials or people on U.S. soil.
world.image_alt: Disclosure of home address helped prompt US Treasury chief

world.title: Iran threatens strikes on U.S. bases in Europe used to attack Tehran
world.summary: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, warned that Iran would strike U.S. bases in Europe or elsewhere if American aircraft used them to attack Iran. He also threatened unspecified distant installations and islands but did not identify targets or say when Iran might strike. A later statem
world.content: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, warned that Iran would strike U.S. bases in Europe or elsewhere if American aircraft used them to attack Iran. He also threatened unspecified distant installations and islands but did not identify targets or say when Iran might strike. A later statement on X said bases involved in an attack would be “legitimate” targets. The war began on Feb. 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region, and armed groups it supports joined the conflict. Tehran has blockaded the Strait of Hormuz and says reopening it depends on U.S. concessions, including lifting sanctions and unfreezing Iranian assets. Qatar and Pakistan have led diplomatic efforts, but disagreements over sanctions, the naval blockade and nuclear issues remain. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Nov. 10 that further attacks were unnecessary, citing economic pressure on Iran. President Donald Trump has also said renewed strikes were unlikely if negotiations progress, while warning that the United States was “locked and loaded” if circumstances change.
world.image_alt: Iran threatens strikes on U.S. bases in Europe used to attack Tehran

world.title: Trump claims victory in Iran war but says U.S. blockade will continue
world.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States had won its war with Iran but wanted a “total victory,” describing the conflict’s end as a matter of when Washington chose to end it. He spoke at a Veterans Day event at Arlington National Cemetery on Nov. 11. U.S. officials have described a pause in major combat and said e
world.content: President Donald Trump said the United States had won its war with Iran but wanted a “total victory,” describing the conflict’s end as a matter of when Washington chose to end it. He spoke at a Veterans Day event at Arlington National Cemetery on Nov. 11. U.S. officials have described a pause in major combat and said economic pressure and negotiations could advance U.S. aims. The war began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28. Washington wants Iran’s enriched uranium removed, while Tehran’s security chief has rejected removing any of it. Iran also demands an end to the U.S. naval blockade and the release of frozen funds. Iran disputes U.S. claims that negotiations are ongoing, and the Strait of Hormuz remains a source of leverage and a risk to commercial shipping. Democrats are set to take control of both chambers of Congress next year, and former U.S. ambassador Ian Kelly said Congress may limit war funding. Britain’s foreign secretary called for intensified diplomacy to end the impasse.
world.image_alt: Trump claims victory in Iran war but says U.S. blockade will continue

world.title: COP31 leaders press climate action as fossil-fuel deal stalls
world.summary: Leaders at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, urged governments on Nov. 11 to keep climate action on the agenda despite wars, trade disputes and soaring energy prices. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries sought agreement on electrification and renewed steps away from fossil fuels. The summit runs through No
world.content: Leaders at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, urged governments on Nov. 11 to keep climate action on the agenda despite wars, trade disputes and soaring energy prices. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries sought agreement on electrification and renewed steps away from fossil fuels. The summit runs through Nov. 20. President Donald Trump and the leaders of China and India are absent, while China sent Vice President Han Zheng. Turkey is promoting a voluntary goal to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, from just over one-fifth now. The proposal does not require the additional electricity to come from clean sources, and governments have yet to agree on a broader plan to cut fossil-fuel use. The European Union says electrification must be clean. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman argued that climate measures should not impede development or compromise energy security, while small-island leaders warned that continued warming threatens their communities. U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres called for a climate justice pact to speed the transition, protect vulnerable communities, secure finance and strengthen international cooperation. He urged governments to tax oil-company windfall profits to help vulnerable countries recover, as negotiations continue toward a final agreement.
world.image_alt: COP31 leaders press climate action as fossil-fuel deal stalls

world.title: Indonesia’s vice president resigns after courts reject education documents
world.summary: Indonesia’s Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted his resignation to the People’s Consultative Assembly on Thursday, Nov. 12, after first sending it to President Prabowo Subianto. His resignation followed court rulings that his overseas education documents did not meet election requirements and a petition by
world.content: Indonesia’s Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted his resignation to the People’s Consultative Assembly on Thursday, Nov. 12, after first sending it to President Prabowo Subianto. His resignation followed court rulings that his overseas education documents did not meet election requirements and a petition by 120 lawmakers from eight political parties that could have led to impeachment proceedings. The assembly has three days to approve the resignation and up to 60 days to elect a successor from two candidates nominated by Prabowo. The vacancy does not trigger a public election. Gibran, 39, is the son of former President Joko Widodo, whose backing helped Prabowo and Gibran win the 2024 election. Analysts have linked the resignation to a widening rift between Prabowo and Widodo. The dispute over Gibran’s eligibility has also renewed criticism of the court ruling that allowed him to run below the usual age threshold.
world.image_alt: Indonesia’s vice president resigns after courts reject education documents

world.title: Israeli strike kills six at Gaza hospital, wounds 20
world.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early Thursday, killing six people and wounding at least 20, Gaza health and civil-defense authorities said. The strike hit the hospital’s surgery department. Medics identified one of the dead as surgeon Rezik Abushira, and footage and reporting by
world.content: An Israeli airstrike hit Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early Thursday, killing six people and wounding at least 20, Gaza health and civil-defense authorities said. The strike hit the hospital’s surgery department. Medics identified one of the dead as surgeon Rezik Abushira, and footage and reporting by an Associated Press journalist at the scene showed extensive damage to the building’s second floor. The Israeli military said it targeted a senior Hamas commander and other members of the group’s armed wing, alleging they were using the hospital as a command center. It said it used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to limit civilian harm. Reuters said it could not independently verify the military’s allegations. Hamas condemned the strike and called for mediators and the U.S. administration to intervene. The attack occurred during a ceasefire that began in October 2025. Gaza health officials say Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,600 Palestinians since the truce took effect, while Israel says four of its soldiers have died during that period. Nasser is among the few medical facilities still functioning in Gaza. The Israeli military said it was reviewing the results of the strike.
world.image_alt: Israeli strike kills six at Gaza hospital, wounds 20

world.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to prisoner swap, but peace talks stall
world.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed in principle to a large prisoner exchange after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi that ended Nov. 11 without a breakthrough on ending the war. The sides had not finalized the number of prisoners or the timing of the exchange. U.S. envoy Jared Kushner called it the largest humanitari
world.content: Russia and Ukraine agreed in principle to a large prisoner exchange after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi that ended Nov. 11 without a breakthrough on ending the war. The sides had not finalized the number of prisoners or the timing of the exchange. U.S. envoy Jared Kushner called it the largest humanitarian release planned in the conflict, while negotiators said major differences remained. The talks addressed postwar security guarantees. Moscow continues to demand that Ukraine withdraw from parts of the eastern Donbas it still controls, while Kyiv rejects surrendering territory and says a ceasefire should precede wider security discussions. U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Kushner are due to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Nov. 12, then travel to Dublin to brief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Washington says it will press to include European representatives in future talks; Russia’s delegation declined to meet European officials in Abu Dhabi.
world.image_alt: Russia and Ukraine agree to prisoner swap, but peace talks stall

world.title: Hoax bomb threats prompt evacuations at 300 Italian schools
world.summary: More than 300 schools in Italy were evacuated Wednesday after bomb-threat emails reached about 6,300 schools; similar messages were sent to schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland. Authorities in all four areas treated the warnings as hoaxes. Italian checks found no suspicious devices or evide
world.content: More than 300 schools in Italy were evacuated Wednesday after bomb-threat emails reached about 6,300 schools; similar messages were sent to schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland. Authorities in all four areas treated the warnings as hoaxes. Italian checks found no suspicious devices or evidence of a concrete danger, and no injuries were reported. The Italian email claimed explosives had been placed in schools and also threatened Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Italy’s education minister, Giuseppe Valditara, said 312 schools had been evacuated, while the education ministry said the messages reached more than 6,300 of Italy’s 7,476 state schools. In Scotland and Northern Ireland, hundreds of schools received threats; police advised against evacuations based solely on the emails, though some Scottish schools briefly evacuated their buildings. Meloni said the threats appeared aimed at causing alarm, and Italian authorities are investigating their origin with European counterparts. Officials have not attributed the school threats to a state or group; Russia has denied allegations of involvement in related disruption campaigns.
world.image_alt: Hoax bomb threats prompt evacuations at 300 Italian schools

business.title: CoreWeave forecast lift sparks AI stock rebound as rate fears persist
business.summary: U.S. technology shares rebounded Wednesday after CoreWeave, a cloud provider of computing capacity for artificial-intelligence workloads, reported stronger-than-expected results and raised its annual revenue forecast. CoreWeave shares jumped 24.7%; the S&P 500 rose 1.3% and the Nasdaq gained 1.6%, recovering some of th
business.content: U.S. technology shares rebounded Wednesday after CoreWeave, a cloud provider of computing capacity for artificial-intelligence workloads, reported stronger-than-expected results and raised its annual revenue forecast. CoreWeave shares jumped 24.7%; the S&P 500 rose 1.3% and the Nasdaq gained 1.6%, recovering some of the previous week’s losses tied to doubts about AI spending and infrastructure expansion. CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, above analysts’ estimate of $3.55 billion, and raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $13 billion-$13.3 billion from $12 billion-$13 billion. Higher-than-expected U.S. inflation has strengthened expectations of Federal Reserve rate increases, which could raise borrowing costs for companies funding data centers with debt. Anthropic’s planned initial public offering is expected next week, Semafor reported.
business.image_alt: CoreWeave forecast lift sparks AI stock rebound as rate fears persist

business.title: U.S. mortgage rates rebound to 7.30% after inflation report
business.summary: U.S. mortgage rates rose Tuesday after four weeks of declines, with the average 30-year fixed rate climbing 12 basis points to 7.30% following a higher-than-expected inflation reading. A separate weekly measure from the Mortgage Bankers Association put the rate at 7.21% for the week ended Nov. 6, down for a fourth stra
business.content: U.S. mortgage rates rose Tuesday after four weeks of declines, with the average 30-year fixed rate climbing 12 basis points to 7.30% following a higher-than-expected inflation reading. A separate weekly measure from the Mortgage Bankers Association put the rate at 7.21% for the week ended Nov. 6, down for a fourth straight week. The recent rate decline had increased demand: mortgage applications rose 6.2% last week, including an 8% increase in home-purchase applications, although purchase applications remained 18% below a year earlier. Higher home prices and borrowing costs continue to weigh on buyers; Realtor.com estimated that buying a median-priced home at a 7.32% mortgage rate would add about $1,100 to the typical mortgage holder’s monthly principal and interest payment.
business.image_alt: U.S. mortgage rates rebound to 7.30% after inflation report

business.title: Tesla extends Cybertruck production through summer 2027 to clear orders
business.summary: Tesla Chief Executive Elon Musk said Wednesday that the company will keep building its Cybertruck electric pickup through the end of summer 2027 to fill more orders. The extension revises a plan announced five days earlier to wind down production around mid-2027 and redirect factory capacity in Texas to the steering-wh
business.content: Tesla Chief Executive Elon Musk said Wednesday that the company will keep building its Cybertruck electric pickup through the end of summer 2027 to fill more orders. The extension revises a plan announced five days earlier to wind down production around mid-2027 and redirect factory capacity in Texas to the steering-wheel-free Cybercab robotaxi. Musk said Cybertruck orders are coming in faster than Tesla can build the vehicles. He had warned that some customers could receive deposit refunds if the line closed before Tesla filled their orders. Tesla still plans to end the truck program and shift capacity to Cybercab; Musk said the extension was less favorable from a profit-maximizing standpoint.
business.image_alt: Tesla extends Cybertruck production through summer 2027 to clear orders

business.title: Nissan cuts sales outlook as China slump hits earnings
business.summary: Nissan Motor cut its global vehicle sales forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to between 2.97 million and 3 million, from 3.15 million, after a sharper-than-expected decline in China. Operating profit for its July-September quarter fell 96% to 2.1 billion yen, while the automaker maintained its full-year ope
business.content: Nissan Motor cut its global vehicle sales forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to between 2.97 million and 3 million, from 3.15 million, after a sharper-than-expected decline in China. Operating profit for its July-September quarter fell 96% to 2.1 billion yen, while the automaker maintained its full-year operating profit and net income targets of 200 billion yen and 20 billion yen, respectively. The company expects China sales to fall to between 370,000 and 400,000 vehicles as weaker demand, faster adoption of new-energy vehicles and tougher competition squeeze its business. Nissan plans to expand exports of China-developed models from two to five and target 12 regional market clusters; it also raised sales forecasts for the United States and Japan. Chief Executive Ivan Espinosa said a new business plan is due in February 2027.
business.image_alt: Nissan cuts sales outlook as China slump hits earnings

business.title: United bars AI agents from booking flights, citing security risks
business.summary: United Airlines said Nov. 11 it will block unauthorized third-party artificial-intelligence agents from booking, changing or managing flights through its digital platforms, travel agencies and booking aggregators. The Chicago-based carrier cited risks to customer credentials, payment details and MileagePlus loyalty acc
business.content: United Airlines said Nov. 11 it will block unauthorized third-party artificial-intelligence agents from booking, changing or managing flights through its digital platforms, travel agencies and booking aggregators. The Chicago-based carrier cited risks to customer credentials, payment details and MileagePlus loyalty accounts, as well as federal aviation and transportation rules requiring travelers to acknowledge safety information themselves during check-in. The updated rules cover ticketing and distribution. United says actions by AI agents could cause unintended purchases, reservation changes or redemptions of miles. The airline can cancel reservations made or managed by AI agents, even if a passenger authorized or supervised the transaction; bookings made before Nov. 11 will be honored. The rules do not prevent customers from using AI to research trips or compare fares, and United tickets remain available through established aggregators. Delta permits authenticated AI assistants to book under safeguards, while Southwest has made flight search available through ChatGPT. United Chief Executive Scott Kirby told The Wall Street Journal he did not want another intermediary between the airline and customers.
business.image_alt: United bars AI agents from booking flights, citing security risks

business.title: Spain strike disrupts factories and transport as businesses dispute impact
business.summary: A 24-hour nationwide strike in Spain disrupted transport and industrial production on Wednesday, with unions reporting stoppages of 90% in automotive and port operations, 85% in meat processing and 75% in energy. Public transport services were curtailed in Barcelona, while Spain’s airport operator AENA said about 5% of
business.content: A 24-hour nationwide strike in Spain disrupted transport and industrial production on Wednesday, with unions reporting stoppages of 90% in automotive and port operations, 85% in meat processing and 75% in energy. Public transport services were curtailed in Barcelona, while Spain’s airport operator AENA said about 5% of flights were canceled. Disruption was less pronounced in retail and restaurants. The scale and economic cost remain disputed. Spain’s main business lobby, CEOE, said most sectors operated normally and called the action a failure, while unions reported strong participation in key industries. BBVA Research chief economist Miguel Cardoso estimated the walkout could reduce Spain’s annual gross domestic product by 0.1% to 0.2%, noting that remote work and the service sector’s growing share of the economy may limit the effect. Spain’s two largest unions and tenants’ groups called the strike to demand housing measures and a new minimum-wage agreement. Businesses say housing shortages also hinder recruitment, but favor increasing construction and cutting taxes rather than expanding market controls. The government is due to ask an interim Parliament on Thursday to approve housing decrees previously rejected by the full chamber.
business.image_alt: Spain strike disrupts factories and transport as businesses dispute impact

business.title: Nvidia loses $450 billion in market value as chip diversion scrutiny intensifies
business.summary: Nvidia lost about $450 billion in market value over two days as scrutiny intensified over whether its advanced chips reached China through Singapore-based customer Megaspeed. The company’s board is investigating reports of Chief Executive Jensen Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Nvidia has said
business.content: Nvidia lost about $450 billion in market value over two days as scrutiny intensified over whether its advanced chips reached China through Singapore-based customer Megaspeed. The company’s board is investigating reports of Chief Executive Jensen Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Nvidia has said it sees no reason to believe secrets were compromised, while Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. Short-seller Culper Research said Megaspeed and its Malaysian affiliate bought $4.8 billion of Nvidia equipment and processors over three years, including $2.9 billion in Nvidia-powered servers in one year. Culper’s figures and diversion allegations have not been established as fact. Nvidia’s market capitalization was reported at more than $4 trillion, and its shares had fallen about 25% from May 13 through Tuesday’s close.
business.image_alt: Nvidia loses $450 billion in market value as chip diversion scrutiny intensifies

business.title: Moody’s raises India’s fiscal 2027 growth forecast to 7%
business.summary: Moody’s Ratings raised its forecast for India’s economic growth in the fiscal year ending March 2027 to 7% from 6.5%, citing strong domestic demand, improving investment and resilience to the energy supply shock linked to the Iran war. The agency expects growth to remain near 7% over the medium term; India’s economy gr
business.content: Moody’s Ratings raised its forecast for India’s economic growth in the fiscal year ending March 2027 to 7% from 6.5%, citing strong domestic demand, improving investment and resilience to the energy supply shock linked to the Iran war. The agency expects growth to remain near 7% over the medium term; India’s economy grew 7.8% from a year earlier in the April-June quarter. Moody’s said India’s diversified crude and gas supplies, state-backed oil companies and tax cuts helped cushion the energy shock. Indicators including capital-goods production, industrial credit and capacity use point to a possible revival in private investment, though tighter monetary policy could delay it. The agency warned that rising prices, weak monsoon conditions and El Niño could weigh on household spending, farm output and rural demand.
business.image_alt: Moody’s raises India’s fiscal 2027 growth forecast to 7%

science.title: Danish study links regular coffee drinking to gut changes
science.summary: A study of 61 healthy Danish adults found that regular coffee drinkers had more diverse gut bacteria, a lower pH in the small intestine and more contractions in the colon than people who drank coffee less often. The observational study cannot establish that coffee caused these differences. Researchers used wireless cap
science.content: A study of 61 healthy Danish adults found that regular coffee drinkers had more diverse gut bacteria, a lower pH in the small intestine and more contractions in the colon than people who drank coffee less often. The observational study cannot establish that coffee caused these differences. Researchers used wireless capsules to record digestive conditions in 50 participants and collected dietary records, urine tests for caffeine metabolites and stool samples. The study was published in Gut Microbiology. Transit time through the digestive tract was similar between the groups. Researchers said they do not yet know whether the lower pH in the small intestine is beneficial or harmful. They said the next step is a controlled intervention study comparing periods of coffee consumption with periods without coffee.
science.image_alt: Danish study links regular coffee drinking to gut changes

science.title: Brazilian wildlife study finds microplastics in remote mammals
science.summary: Researchers found microplastics in blood samples from 43 of 47 lowland tapirs and giant anteaters studied across Brazil, with concentrations averaging 73.8 particles per milliliter. The team combined blood testing with GPS tracking of the animals’ movements and found higher concentrations in animals whose habitats had
science.content: Researchers found microplastics in blood samples from 43 of 47 lowland tapirs and giant anteaters studied across Brazil, with concentrations averaging 73.8 particles per milliliter. The team combined blood testing with GPS tracking of the animals’ movements and found higher concentrations in animals whose habitats had more human disturbance or were closer to development and waste facilities. Researchers also detected microplastics in animals in the Pantanal more than 65 kilometers from settlements and 112 kilometers from a waste facility. They say the particles may reach remote habitats through air and water, but the study cannot establish their source or prove that human activity directly caused the contamination. The study did not assess health effects in the animals; the researchers say further work is needed to determine how the particles reach wildlife and what effects they have.
science.image_alt: Brazilian wildlife study finds microplastics in remote mammals

science.title: COP31 climate finance pledges fall 71% as key donors hold back
science.summary: Developed countries’ public climate-finance pledges for the coming years have fallen about 71% to roughly $11.7 billion a year, as most major donors let previous commitments expire without announcing replacements at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye. The funding is intended to help developing countries cut e
science.content: Developed countries’ public climate-finance pledges for the coming years have fallen about 71% to roughly $11.7 billion a year, as most major donors let previous commitments expire without announcing replacements at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye. The funding is intended to help developing countries cut emissions and prepare for climate impacts. The shortfall in announced public funding is also making it harder for recipient governments to plan and attract private investment. Countries agreed at COP29 to a target of $300 billion a year by 2035. An analysis cited by The Guardian says developed countries could be broadly on track if existing contributions continue. The United States is not expected to provide official climate finance, while Germany, France and Japan have not announced new multi-year pledges. COP31 runs through Nov. 20.
science.image_alt: COP31 climate finance pledges fall 71% as key donors hold back

science.title: European Hera probe begins examining asteroid struck in NASA deflection test
science.summary: The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft has begun surveying the Didymos asteroid pair from about 25 to 30 kilometers away, four years after NASA deliberately struck the smaller asteroid, Dimorphos, to test asteroid deflection. Hera’s first images show Didymos from a new angle, revealing boulders, craters and ridge-
science.content: The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft has begun surveying the Didymos asteroid pair from about 25 to 30 kilometers away, four years after NASA deliberately struck the smaller asteroid, Dimorphos, to test asteroid deflection. Hera’s first images show Didymos from a new angle, revealing boulders, craters and ridge-like features; some rocks may have been blasted from Dimorphos and traveled about 1 kilometer to the larger asteroid. The 2022 impact shortened Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by about 32 to 33 minutes and also altered the pair’s path around the sun. Hera’s close-up investigation aims to determine how the impact changed Dimorphos and why the deflection was greater than simulations predicted. The probe is expected to begin closer, more detailed observations next month, using 25 instruments and two CubeSats that will survey Dimorphos and attempt to land there.
science.image_alt: European Hera probe begins examining asteroid struck in NASA deflection test

science.title: Mantle-driven uplift explains Earth
science.summary: A new model suggests slow circulation in Earth’s mantle lifted parts of three ancient continental regions, allowing ice sheets to erode rock layers and create the Great Unconformity, a gap in the geological record. The study by University of Wollongong researchers Santosh Dhungana and Nicolas Flament was published Nov.
science.content: A new model suggests slow circulation in Earth’s mantle lifted parts of three ancient continental regions, allowing ice sheets to erode rock layers and create the Great Unconformity, a gap in the geological record. The study by University of Wollongong researchers Santosh Dhungana and Nicolas Flament was published Nov. 4 in Nature. The model indicates Laurentia, Baltica and North China rose from roughly a billion years ago to about 540 million years ago, then began sinking, allowing younger sediments to accumulate. Flament said glaciation likely drove much of the erosion, but mantle uplift created the slopes glaciers needed to carry sediment away.

science.title: COP31 leaders debate fossil fuel exit as US skips summit
science.summary: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres urged governments at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya on Wednesday to set clear timetables for moving away from fossil fuels, warning that climate action is falling behind. Türkiye is hosting the talks, scheduled through Nov. 20, with delegations from nearly 200 coun
science.content: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres urged governments at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya on Wednesday to set clear timetables for moving away from fossil fuels, warning that climate action is falling behind. Türkiye is hosting the talks, scheduled through Nov. 20, with delegations from nearly 200 countries seeking agreement on climate measures. Türkiye is promoting a voluntary target to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. The proposal does not require that new electricity come from clean sources. The European Union has said electrification must be clean, while the role of coal, oil and gas remains contested. The United States sent no official delegation for a second consecutive year under President Donald Trump, while leaders of several other major countries also stayed away. Negotiators are trying to revive stalled talks on phasing out fossil fuels after the previous summit in Brazil failed to reach consensus on a global plan.
science.image_alt: COP31 leaders debate fossil fuel exit as US skips summit

science.title: Historic US ocean liner sinks off Florida to become world
science.summary: The retired SS United States, once the world’s fastest ocean liner, was sunk off Florida’s Gulf Coast on Nov. 11 to become the world’s largest artificial reef. The 990-foot ship took several hours to descend, leaning to one side before disappearing beneath the water around 10 p.m. The $13.5 million project aims to crea
science.content: The retired SS United States, once the world’s fastest ocean liner, was sunk off Florida’s Gulf Coast on Nov. 11 to become the world’s largest artificial reef. The 990-foot ship took several hours to descend, leaning to one side before disappearing beneath the water around 10 p.m. The $13.5 million project aims to create marine habitat and attract divers and fishing enthusiasts to Okaloosa County. Before the sinking, crews removed fuel and other potentially hazardous materials, opened sections of the hull and decks to let water enter, and cut passages to allow marine life to move through the structure. The ship will rest in about 180 feet of water, with its upper decks roughly 50 to 60 feet below the surface. The ship’s conversion followed years of failed preservation efforts and rising costs to keep it docked in Philadelphia. Okaloosa County bought it in 2024; plans call for the removed smokestacks to be used at a museum honoring the liner.
science.image_alt: Historic US ocean liner sinks off Florida to become world

science.title: Study finds BMI misses obesity cases, misclassifies others across four countries
science.summary: An international study of 844,108 adults in China, the United Kingdom, the United States and Spain found that using body measurements alongside body mass index (BMI) to diagnose obesity identified 3.3% to 7.4% more cases than BMI alone. The researchers tested a framework proposed by a Lancet commission in 2025 that add
science.content: An international study of 844,108 adults in China, the United Kingdom, the United States and Spain found that using body measurements alongside body mass index (BMI) to diagnose obesity identified 3.3% to 7.4% more cases than BMI alone. The researchers tested a framework proposed by a Lancet commission in 2025 that adds measures such as waist circumference and distinguishes clinical obesity, in which excess fat impairs bodily function, from preclinical obesity, in which it poses a risk without current dysfunction. Compared with the expanded framework, BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2% to 3.1% of participants and missed it in 5.2% to 8.6%. Clinical obesity was associated with a 69% higher risk of death than no obesity, while 77% to 91% of people with preclinical obesity did not progress to the clinical form within 10 years. Researchers and clinicians said the added assessments could help target care, but require more detailed evaluation than BMI measurement alone.
science.image_alt: Study finds BMI misses obesity cases, misclassifies others across four countries

sports.title: Sri Lanka centuries cut Pakistan
sports.summary: Sri Lanka’s Dhananjaya de Silva and captain Kusal Mendis scored unbeaten centuries to take their side to 404-4 on day three of the first Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi, 30 runs behind Pakistan’s first-innings total of 434-9 declared. De Silva was 167 not out and Mendis 117 not out, with their unbroken stand worth
sports.content: Sri Lanka’s Dhananjaya de Silva and captain Kusal Mendis scored unbeaten centuries to take their side to 404-4 on day three of the first Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi, 30 runs behind Pakistan’s first-innings total of 434-9 declared. De Silva was 167 not out and Mendis 117 not out, with their unbroken stand worth 249 runs. Sri Lanka had resumed at 114-3 and scored 290 runs during the day. Pakistan had taken three early wickets in Sri Lanka’s reply but managed only one on day three. Pakistan fast bowler Mohammad Abbas dismissed Kamindu Mendis for 58, while bad light ended play with 23 overs still unbowled. Sri Lanka were looking to build a first-innings lead when play was due to resume on Thursday, Nov. 12. The first Test is scheduled to run through Nov. 13.

sports.title: Rams hold Puka Nacua off injured reserve as receivers recover

Nacua was hurt on the final offensive play of the Rams’ Nov. 8 win over Washington; the team cited roster-management considerations for keepi
sports.content: Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that wide receiver Puka Nacua will not go on injured reserve despite knee sprains and turf toe, but will miss an extended period. Nacua was hurt on the final offensive play of the Rams’ Nov. 8 win over Washington; the team cited roster-management considerations for keeping him off the list. Los Angeles is also without wide receiver Davante Adams, who has been sidelined by a ruptured hamstring since Week 6. McVay said a return for Adams after the Rams’ Nov. 25 game against Green Bay was realistic, potentially putting him back for the Dec. 3 game against Kansas City. The Rams did not add a receiver at the trade deadline, saying the available deals were too costly and that they expect Adams back; Nacua could return around Weeks 14 or 15. Los Angeles visits Arizona next, followed by its Week 11 bye.

Both won in their first full major-league seasons after debuting in 202
sports.content: Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski and New York Yankees starter Cam Schlittler each received all 30 first-place votes to win the National League and American League Cy Young Awards, baseball’s top pitching honors, announced Wednesday, Nov. 11. Both won in their first full major-league seasons after debuting in 2025. Misiorowski, 24, went 16-5 with a major-league-best 1.80 earned-run average and 252 strikeouts; Schlittler, 25, went 14-6 with an AL-best 1.95 ERA and 239 strikeouts. Misiorowski won the award after helping Milwaukee win its first World Series championship. His 105.5 mph fastball set a record for a starting pitcher in the tracking era, and he threw 5⅔ scoreless innings as the starter in the title-clinching Game 5. The Yankees reached the American League Division Series, where Tampa Bay eliminated them. The awards recognize regular-season performance: voters submitted ballots before the postseason began. The Baseball Writers’ Association of America also announced its first Reliever of the Year awards. The league Most Valuable Player winners are scheduled to be announced Thursday, Nov. 12.

sports.content: Quarterback Kirk Cousins has rejoined the Minnesota Vikings and begun preparing for Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers, as coach Kevin O’Connell weighs whether he is ready to start. The 6-2 Vikings brought back their former starter from the Las Vegas Raiders to steady a struggling offense. Cousins, 38, said a call with O’Connell helped persuade him to accept the trade after the teams agreed on compensation. He wanted a familiar offense rather than “completely starting over” and said O’Connell understood his strengths and limitations. Cousins passed for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in nine starts for the Raiders this season. O’Connell said Minnesota is preparing for Cousins to start but has not made a final decision, citing the need to get him comfortable with the playbook. Cousins said Wednesday it was too early to give a firm answer. The matchup would bring him back to Lambeau Field, where he suffered an Achilles injury in the final game of his previous Vikings tenure.

sports.title: Former NFL coach Rex Ryan faces six charges after Nashville crash
sports.summary: Former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills coach Rex Ryan, now an ESPN football analyst, turned himself in to Nashville police on Nov. 11 after authorities accused him of striking two pedestrians with his pickup truck and leaving the scene. Police said the pedestrians had the right of way at a downtown intersection on Nov.
sports.content: Former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills coach Rex Ryan, now an ESPN football analyst, turned himself in to Nashville police on Nov. 11 after authorities accused him of striking two pedestrians with his pickup truck and leaving the scene. Police said the pedestrians had the right of way at a downtown intersection on Nov. 5 when Ryan turned and drove over their feet; they suffered minor injuries. He faces six misdemeanor counts: two each of leaving an accident scene, failing to provide information or aid, and failing to obey a traffic signal. A judicial commissioner set bond at $6,000, but Ryan qualified for release on nonfinancial conditions. His attorney, David Raybin, said Ryan surrendered after learning of the charges and intended to cooperate as the case proceeds. Ryan is scheduled to appear in court on Dec. 18, according to a local report. ESPN said it was aware of the case and in contact with Ryan; the network had not decided whether to take disciplinary action while it gathered information.

sports.content: Mirra Andreeva, the 19-year-old French Open champion, beat world No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Wednesday, winning 11 straight games after trailing 1-4 to reach the semifinals as Group 2 winner. The match lasted 62 minutes. Sabalenka must now beat Elina Svitolina in Friday’s final group match to claim the other semifinal berth. Svitolina recovered from a set down to defeat Karolina Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2, setting up Friday’s decider. The Ukrainian took an eight-minute medical timeout after the first set before turning the match around. Andreeva’s subsequent win over Sabalenka eliminated Muchova. Andreeva has won both group matches without dropping a set, while Sabalenka and Svitolina enter Friday’s decider with one win apiece. The tournament debutant has secured her place in the last four with a group match to spare; the winner of Sabalenka–Svitolina will join her there.

sports.content: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry defended his wife, actor and entrepreneur Ayesha Curry, on Nov. 11 after former athletes criticized her for taking a leading role and sharing a scripted kiss with co-star Matthew Daddario in the romantic comedy Second Chance Holiday. The film premiered on The Roku Channel on Nov. 5, marking Ayesha Curry’s first leading role in a feature film. Stephen Curry said the remarks diminished her professional achievement and reflected restrictive views of what women should be allowed to do. Former NBA guard Gilbert Arenas called Ayesha Curry the “only blemish” in her husband’s family and contrasted her public profile with the quieter roles he associated with other star players’ wives. Former Warriors teammate Nick Young also joined the podcast discussion. Former NFL players Emmanuel Acho and LeSean McCoy separately questioned her decision to take the role. Young apologized to Stephen Curry after Curry posted his response, while Arenas said he was sorry if Curry was offended but continued to defend his remarks. Ayesha Curry also responded to the viral scene, writing that it was not real.

sports.content: England captain Harry Kane is set to become the team’s most-capped men’s player when he makes his 126th appearance against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, November 12. He will surpass former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, whose record of 125 caps has stood since 1990. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker already holds England’s scoring record with 91 goals and won the 2026 Ballon d’Or last month. England manager Thomas Tuchel confirmed Kane will start and said the Ballon d’Or will be presented to supporters before the match. Kane described the caps milestone as one of the biggest of his career, crediting the work behind the scenes that keeps him fit. Since joining Bayern from Tottenham in 2023, he has scored 156 goals for the German club and won Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026. Kane is still pursuing a major international trophy. England’s last men’s title came at the 1966 World Cup, and the team lost European Championship finals in 2021 and 2024 before reaching the 2026 World Cup semi-finals. Kane says he wants to reach 100 England goals and has not ruled out another World Cup campaign in 2030. England conclude their Nations League group against Spain on Sunday.
